sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the advantage of Malchus through the aspect of "Kol" involves both the flow of Yesod and the higher influx of the fifty gates of Binah, which are beyond the emotions and relate to the self rather than to others.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the maamar,
that this that the sefirah of Yesod is called by the name "Kol" (all) is because of the fifty gates of Binah that are drawn into it
(Kol in gematria equals fifty).
And from this it is understood,
that the advantage in "Eretz" (land)
(Malchus)
through the aspect of "Kol" is in two matters.
That Yesod is drawn into it,
which is the conclusion of the emotions of Atzilus,
and furthermore,
that through Yesod the fifty gates of Binah are drawn into it,
intellect that is above the emotions.
And it can be said,
that these two matters are related to each other.
And the explanation is,
that emotions are related to another.
For although the emotions are a matter that pertains to the person himself
(and not like speech, which is a revelation to another),
nevertheless,
they are at the level of the person as he relates to another,
and the intellect is at the level of the person as he is to himself,
separate from another.
Therefore,
when the flow is only from the aspect of the emotions of Z'eir Anpin, which are related to another,
then,
by Malchus receiving within itself the emotions of Z'eir Anpin, a change occurs in it
(as above in section 3),
and this that Malchus receives the emotions of Z'eir Anpin as they are
[for this is the matter of "the advantage of the land in all is a king,"
that also in the land the revelation of the aspect of "Kol" shines as it is in its essence],
is through the root of the flow being from the intellect,
for since the intellect is above relation to another
(the matter of speech,
Malchus),
therefore,
even when the flow comes into speech,
speech does not have the ability to effect a change in it.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the revelation of the aspect of the "Supernal King" through mitzvos is above even the level of Sovev (the encompassing light), which still relates to worlds, and is from the Essence of the Ein Sof.

translations.translation: And behold, even the intellect that is above relation to another is within the order of Hishtalshelus (the chain of descent).
And the revelation of the aspect of the "Supernal King" that comes through the fulfillment of the mitzvos
("a king is subjugated to the field")
is above the aspect of "Kol,"
it is above Hishtalshelus.
And to add,
according to what is explained elsewhere
that "Kol" is the aspect of Sovev (the encompassing light),
and this that Yesod is called by the name "Kol" is because Yesod is in the central line that reaches to Kesser
(Sovev)
[and this is what is written,
"For all in heaven and on earth," and it is translated as "that holds heaven and earth,"
for regarding Sovev, heaven and earth are equal],
it must be said,
that the revelation of the aspect of the "Supernal King"
(through the fulfillment of the mitzvos)
is above even the aspect of Sovev.
For Sovev is related to worlds, except that it is above them and encompasses them all as one.
And this is "For all in heaven and on earth,"
that even regarding Sovev there is heaven and earth,
except that it connects and unifies them—"that holds heaven and earth."
And through the mitzvos, there is a drawing down of the revelation of the Essence of the Ein Sof, which is above relation to worlds,
above even Sovev.
And as explained in the maamar,
that the flow through the fulfillment of the mitzvos is from the pnimiyus (innerness) of Kesser.
And the distinction between Arich
(the externality of Kesser)
and Atik
(the pnimiyus of Kesser)
is,
that Arich is the root and source of the emanated beings, except that it encompasses them—Sovev,
and Atik is a lower level within the Emanator—the Ein Sof that is above relation to worlds.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that specifically Tiferes, the central emotion, draws from the innerness of Kesser, while Yesod draws from the encompassing root of the emanated beings.

translations.translation: And it is explained in the maamar,
that "Supernal King" is Tiferes
[as it is stated in the Zohar there, "King" refers to the Holy One, Blessed be He,
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, is the aspect of Tiferes]
and Tiferes draws from the pnimiyus of Kesser.
And it can be said,
that this that specifically Tiferes
(specifically)
draws from the pnimiyus of Kesser,
even though Yesod is also in the central line,
is,
because Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes are the essence of the emotions, and Netzach, Hod, and Yesod are that through which the influence is transmitted
(of the emotions of Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferes),
therefore,
the revelation of Kesser through Yesod
(through which the influence is transmitted)
is the aspect of the root of the emanated beings,
and the revelation of Kesser through Tiferes
(which is above influence)
is the aspect of the pnimiyus of Kesser.
